To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
We engaged in a design process with a larp designer, and created a set of social wearables, embedded in a larp, that supported social engagement and co-experience values.

1) larp designers have an understanding of how to craft experiences that support social engagement; 2) larp designers are able to transfer this understanding to the design of social wearable technology; and 3) the design affordances that larp designers use in crafting social experiences resonate with values of collocated social engagement

(1) larpers' values and experiences are a valuable source of inspiration for designing social wearables that support collocated engagement; (2) larpers are a valuable source for co-designing and evaluating such wearables; and (3) the resulting social wearbles are valuable in the larping community.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how social wearables can be designed in support of social engagement.
designing social wearables for collocated engagement.
designing future social wearables that support collocated engagement and physical and social interaction in a playful context.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have shown that the values of the LARP community can be translated to the design of social wearable technology.
this paper presents the results of a co-design process between larp designers and HCI researchers that led to the creation of social wearables for larp.
the design process with the larp designers resulted in the design of social wearable that support collocated engagement.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are interested in the design of social technologies, and that we are interested to learn from larpers and lars designers.
we have shown how a larp designer's expertise in creating social engagement can be used in designing social wearables.
larp designers can be a valuable source of inspiration for wearable technology designers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
social wearables should not be designed as stand-alone artifacts, but rather as part of a larger system that includes the physical and social environment.

larp designers can be a valuable source of inspiration when designing social wearables that support collocated engagement, as they have a long tradition of designing and crafting elements that support co-experience values, and are familiar with designing for social engagement in collocated settings.
social wearables can be designed to support co-experience by providing a shared experience of the body, a shared physical experience of objects, and by providing a shared narrative experience.
